19.2 Write the order-independence proper.failingExample:
seed=6594 iter=4 pattern=pii_ssn ref=(77,88). Minimal reproducer: scan("4155552671 123-45-6789") == (pii_phone@0..10,) only — the SSN 123-45-6789 at (11,22) is confirmable alone but dropped. Also scan("4155552671 4111111111111111") drops the valid card at (11,27).

Root cause: the phone prefilter `(?:\+?\d[\s().\-]?){9,14}\d` over-consumes past the precise end — on "4155552671 123-45-6789" it matches (0,17)="4155552671 123-45" while the phone PRECISE confirms only (0,10). Because the precise confirm SUCCEEDS at (0,10), matcher.scan does NOT enter the failed-region rescan; the primary _COMBINED.finditer then resumes at the prefilter match end (17), skipping the SSN start at 11 entirely. The gap [precise_end, prefilter_end) after a SUCCESSFUL confirm is never rescanned, so a confirmable match of another pattern inside that gap is lost. This violates design Property 6 ("every match a single pattern P would confirm ALONE SHALL either appear in scan(text) or lie inside the span of a match of another pattern that scan confirmed"): the dropped SSN is neither emitted nor contained in any emitted span.

The test is written to design.md Property 6 verbatim and is independent of the matcher internals (a frozen single-pattern reference built from RULESET[name].prefilter/.precise/.validator + local Luhn). The shipped GW09 test_property6 does NOT catch this because its _reference_scan reproduces matcher.scan's exact algorithm (rescan only on failed confirm) and asserts scan==reference, so both skip the same gap. 5 of 6 tests in the file pass (Property 5 section + the structural one-primary-pass invariant). The matcher fix (task 18.4) only rescans FAILED-confirm regions; it does not rescan the trailing gap left by a prefilter that over-consumes past a SUCCESSFUL precise confirm.
